question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Colonial educational institution and its location/year of establishment]
options: University of Calcutta — Calcutta; established 1857, first modern university in India
University of Punjab — Lahore; established 1857 along with the three Presidency universities
wrong_fact: The University of Punjab was established in 1882 in Lahore, NOT in 1857. The three universities established simultaneously in 1857 were Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras — following Wood's Despatch (1854). Punjab University came 25 years later.
explanation: The Universities of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras were all established in 1857 following Charles Wood's Education Despatch of 1854 — this is correct for all three options. The University of Punjab (Lahore) was established in 1882, a full 25 years later. Grouping it with the 1857 universities is a factual historical error.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Colonial educational reformer/policy and its primary impact region]
options: Alexander Duff — Calcutta; introduced English-medium higher education combining Western knowledge with evangelical goals (from 1830)
Charles Wood's Despatch (1854) — British India; recommended universities in Presidency towns and a network of vernacular schools
Thomas Munro's Presidency School Survey (1822–26) — Madras Presidency; documented traditional indigenous education institutions (pathshalas, madrasas)
Lord Curzon's Universities Act (1904) — primarily targeting the University of Punjab; aimed to increase government control over higher education
wrong_fact: Lord Curzon's Indian Universities Act (1904) was aimed primarily at the University of Calcutta and other Indian universities broadly — NOT primarily or specifically at Punjab University. The Calcutta University was the main focus, as it had a large number of affiliated colleges and was seen as a hotbed of nationalist sentiment.
explanation: Alexander Duff's English-medium education mission in Calcutta (from 1830) is historically accurate. Wood's Despatch (1854) recommending presidency universities and vernacular schools is correctly described. Munro's survey of indigenous education in Madras Presidency (1822–26) is a historically documented fact. The error is in option 4 — Curzon's 1904 Universities Act was directed at Calcutta and Indian universities broadly, targeting the University of Calcutta in particular, not Punjab University specifically.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Institution/initiative and its location and significance in colonial education history]
options: Fort William College (1800) — Calcutta; established by Lord Wellesley to train British civil servants in Indian languages
Elphinstone College (1827) — Bombay; founded from funds contributed by Indians honouring Governor Mountstuart Elphinstone
Presidency College, Madras (1840) — Madras; evolved from the Madras Preparatory School under the Madras Literary Society
Banaras Hindu University (1916) — Varanasi; founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya with support of Annie Besant and the Theosophical Society as co-founders
wrong_fact: Banaras Hindu University (1916) was founded primarily by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya. Annie Besant was NOT a co-founder. Annie Besant founded the separate Central Hindu College (1898) in Varanasi, which was later merged into BHU — but Besant and the Theosophical Society are not credited as co-founders of BHU itself. Besant actually later had disputes over the merger of her college into BHU.
explanation: Fort William College (1800) by Lord Wellesley in Calcutta is correctly matched. Elphinstone College (1827) in Bombay with funds contributed by Indian merchants honouring Elphinstone is historically accurate. Presidency College Madras evolving from earlier institutions is correct. The error in option 4 is describing Annie Besant and the Theosophical Society as co-founders of BHU (1916) — Malaviya was the founder; Besant's Central Hindu College (1898) was merged into BHU but she was not a BHU co-founder and actually opposed certain aspects of the merger.
